Subject: Hosting options and expected sizing for regulatory pilot

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As mentioned, Crestview (clinical genomics) needs a recommended hosting posture for a pilot tied to our upcoming contract: we have strict PHI controls and expect 1.2M tokens/day after month 3, spiking to 2.8M on heavy inference days. We need your suggestion between Dedicated (Redwood Reserved) and Private (VPC/on-prem) for the pilot that will later scale to a production tenancy.

Key ask: can you provide a short recommendation that includes: GPU slate (types & counts), expected 95th p50/p95 latency for typical prompts (1k tokens), cost delta between Dedicated vs Private for the pilot (3 months), and what the procurement timeline looks like if we choose Private?

Liam
Head of Platform
Crestview Labs

Subject: Re: Hosting options and expected sizing for regulatory pilot

Hi Liam — appreciated the discussion. Below is a concise starter recommendation; Rishi will add technical sizing details and Vivek will confirm contractual/discount flexibility.

Executive summary (short):
- Recommended: Start pilot on Dedicated Reserved capacity (private VLAN, customer-only pool) with a clear escape path to Private if Crestview requires air-gapped/on-prem later. Dedicated gives fastest time-to-value and predictable throughput while meeting isolation requirements for pilot workloads.
- Pilot slate: 4x H100-80GB (pin to a private pool) with 2:1 burst credit to handle spiky days; KV prefix cache enabled for common prompts.
- Latency: expected median ~90ms/token, p95 ~210ms/token for 1k-token prompts on H100-80GB with batching and KV caching.
- Cost delta (est): Dedicated ~25% lower upfront procurement friction vs Private for a 3-month pilot; Private has higher one-time onboarding + infra cost but lower long-run unit cost if Crestview purchases and amortizes hardware.

Next steps: Rishi to surface detailed GPU sizing and fallback plan; I’ll add commercial terms and timeline. Can we agree on a quick MAP (mutual action plan) this week?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Liam / Aditya — adding the technical sizing and a concrete comparison table so you have something to share with procurement. High-level assumptions: 1k-token average requests, 120k requests/day steady-state (1.2M tokens/day), 280k request spike (2.8M tokens/day) expected during batch processing windows. Using a modern opt model (redwood-rlhf-13b equivalent) quantized (int8/nn) for Dedicated/Private.

Dedicated recommendation (pilot):
- Hardware: 4x NVIDIA H100-80GB (or 8x A10G if cost-constrained — A10G gives ~60-70% throughput relative to H100 for our model)
- Config: 2 inference workers per GPU, pinned KV cache per worker, continuous batching with max latency target 250ms
- Throughput: baseline steady 120k req/day -> requires ~2.5 H100-equivalents sustained; 4x H100 provides ~1.6x headroom for spikes and background retraining/ops tasks.
- Observability: token-level billing + per-route p95 tracer enabled.
- Failover: automatic routing to a lower-cost variant (quantized lower-precision) if Dedicated pool capacity saturated; fall back to a regional Dedicated pool in another AZ for redundancy.
- Estimated pilot monthly run-rate (infra only): $95k/month (Dedicated reserved monthly amortization & infra), 3-month pilot ~ $285k (excluding negotiated credits).

Private (on-prem/VPC) option:
- Hardware: recommend 6x H100-80GB to provide similar headroom (no cloud bursting), plus spare node for maintenance -> total 7 nodes procured or via a 12-month amortization plan.
- Ops: longer onboarding (~6-8 weeks), network setup, KMS/HSM integration, and SOC audit time.
- Latency: slightly lower p50/p95 for colocated on-prem workloads (p95 improvement ~10-15ms) but operational risk higher early on.
- Estimated one-time procurement + setup for pilot: ~$1.1M (hardware + rack + networking + certified install); monthly ops ~ $40k/month; 3-month cost > $1.2M total (significantly higher than Dedicated pilot).

Tradeoffs / recommendation rationale:
- If the primary constraint is time-to-revenue and predictable cost for the pilot: Dedicated Reserved is the right path.
- If Crestview requires explicit air-gapped guarantees for production and can commit to long-term hardware amortization (12–36 months), Private becomes economical beyond ~9–12 months.

Technical addenda:
- GPU slate decision matrix attached (H100 vs A10G benchmark). See H100-vs-A10-benchmark.pdf.
- KV cache sizing: plan for ~40GB per worker for common prompt sets; this was sized from your shared prompt list.

Happy to walk through numbers with procurement; I can also run a PoC on an A10G pool if you want a lower-cost pilot.

— Rishi
Principal Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference
